touches.text: The ticket IS its own manager. It carries its workflow and status, and asks each gate whether it can transit. If refused, it gets itself back to design for fixing. If no handler is available to ask, it throws a trouble and waits until we decide. Design is CC and Akien. Akien, 2026-11-11, Q#85: "you and me. later there will be a specific agent for it, but that's so far off we're not even thinking about it now except 'after the outline is implemented'." So until then a refused ticket waits in the trouble lane, which both of us read when a session opens, and nothing posts to a design verb that no machine answers.
The ticket owns its refusals: a gate refuses a crossing on the ticket's behalf. The gates are CodeMother's (9.3.5).

Once build_inspector moves into CodeMother, code outside her reaches it over the bus: the 18 crossing calls in transitions.py, the other code sites and the 82 proofs that run a sieve over themselves. No published client tool, no fifth exception. Akien 2026-11-13, on Q#88: "over the bus. that's what it's for?"
gate: the == compare, in one place. A gate opens when every expected equals its actual. No oracle, ever.
Entry gates exist only to kick back what doesn't meet the entry requirements. Nothing in them is about who writes what.

The inspectors are not assumed correct; they are examined when they refuse. After a gate refuses, an LLM sets the refusing sieve's intention and why beside the ticket's intention and why and asks: is this sieve the best we can do right now? If yes, the ticket changes. If no, the sieve is fixed through its own ticket and proof. Either way the system improves. WHY: a disagreement becomes an update to an intention or its implementation, never a conversation about procedure. The sieves stay deterministic and never weigh a why; the LLM check comes only after a failure, and it is never a lock pick because it has no third outcome. Nothing passes a ticket over a red.
A sieve's rule follows the ticket's kind, read off the ticket, so it stays deterministic; 17.11.6 is left for what the rules do not cover.
